ArrangementCalculator.count:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the number of permutations of n items taken m at a time, treating a missing m or m equal to n as selecting all items." count]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> n </REF>: int "Total number of items."
        <REF> m </REF>: int or None "Number of items to arrange; may be None to select all items."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: int "The number of permutations as an integer."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the condition m is None or n == m using left-to-right short-circuit. RESULT branch_condition]
            [COMMAND Execute the matching branch and return the computed permutation count. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: m is None or n == m evaluates to true]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return ArrangementCalculator.factorial(n). RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: m is not None and n != m evaluates to true]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the floor division of ArrangementCalculator.factorial(n) by ArrangementCalculator.factorial(n - m). RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArrangementCalculator.count_all:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Sums ArrangementCalculator.count(n, i) for every integer i from 1 through n inclusive and returns the accumulated total." count_all]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> n </REF>: int "Upper inclusive bound for the loop and first argument passed to ArrangementCalculator.count."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> total </REF>: int "The sum of ArrangementCalculator.count(n, i) for i from 1 through n inclusive."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize total to 0. RESULT total]
            [COMMAND For each i from 1 to n inclusive, add ArrangementCalculator.count(n, i) to total. RESULT total]
            [COMMAND Return total. RESULT total]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArrangementCalculator.select:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Returns all permutations of length m from self.datas as a list of lists, defaulting m to the length of self.datas when none is provided." select]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> m </REF>: int or None "The desired permutation length; defaults to len(self.datas) when None."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: list "A list of all generated permutations, each represented as a list."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND If m is None, assign m = len(self.datas); otherwise keep the provided m unchanged. RESULT m]
            [COMMAND Initialize result to an empty list. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND For each permutation tuple generated by itertools.permutations(self.datas, m), convert the tuple to a list and append it to result. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Return the populated result list. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArrangementCalculator.select_all:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Collects all items from self.datas by calling self.select(i) for every index i from 1 to len(self.datas) inclusive and returning the combined list." select_all]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: list "A list containing the concatenated results of self.select(i) for all i from 1 to len(self.datas) inclusive."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize an empty list named result. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND For each i from 1 to len(self.datas) inclusive, call self.select(i) and extend result with the returned elements. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Return result. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
ArrangementCalculator.factorial:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the factorial of n by accumulating the product of integers from 2 through n inclusive, returning 1 for n less than 2." factorial]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> n </REF>: int "The integer input whose factorial is computed."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: int "The computed factorial of n; equals 1 when n is less than 2 because the loop does not execute."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize result to the constant value 1. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND For each integer i from 2 through n inclusive, multiply result by i and assign the product back to result. If n is less than 2, execute zero loop iterations and leave result as 1. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Return the accumulated result. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
